mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted, {سُورَة أنزلناها}: سورة is made nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "this is a sūra" (هَذِه سُورَة), and أنزلناها is a description (ṣifa) of سورة. An implied mubtadaʾ was needed, and سورة was not made nominative as a mubtadaʾ itself, only because it is indefinite, and one does not begin with an indefinite noun unless it is qualified; and if you make {أنزلناها} an adjective (naʿt), there would be no khabar (predicate) for it in the speech, because the adjective of a mubtadaʾ cannot be its khabar. So there was no avoiding implying a mubtadaʾ so that the qualification of السورة by أنزلناها would be sound.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read سُورَةً أنزلناها in the accusative, by an implied verb which أنزلناها explains, its implied form being "We sent down a sūra — We sent it down" (أنزلنَا سُورَة أنزلناها). On this reading أنزلناها may not be a description of سورة, because a description does not explain what governs the described noun, just as the ṣila does not explain what governs the described [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense requires "the relative (mawṣūl)"]. It is also said that the accusative is on the implied form "recite a sūra which We have sent down" (اتل سُورَة أنزلناها); on this interpretation it is good for أنزلناها to be an adjective of السورة, because it does not explain the governor of السورة.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {إِن الَّذين جاؤوا بالإفك عصبَة}: عصبة is the khabar of إن. It is permissible to read it in the accusative, and then the khabar is {لكل امْرِئ مِنْهُم}.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {أَن تعودوا}: أن is in the position of the accusative by the omission of the preposition, its implied form being "so that you do not return" (لئلا تعودوا) or "out of aversion to your returning" (كَرَاهَة أَن تعودوا); so it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying {الزَّانِيَة وَالزَّانِي فاجلدوا كل وَاحِد مِنْهُمَا}: the preferred reading according to Sībawayh is the nominative, because by that two specific individuals are not intended. So the nominative, according to Sībawayh, is as a mubtadaʾ (subject) on the assumption of an omitted khabar (predicate), its implied form being "among what has been made obligatory upon you is [the case of] the fornicatress and the fornicator; so flog…" (فِيمَا فرض عَلَيْكُم الزَّانِيَة وَالزَّانِي فاجلدوا). It is also said that the khabar is what follows it, namely فاجلدوا, as you say زيد فاضربه ("Zayd — strike him"), as though the fāʾ were redundant (zāʾida).
It has been read بأربعةٍ شهداءَ, and this is irregular (shādhdh); شهداء would then be a naʿt (adjective) of أربعة, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from an indefinite noun.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying {دينهم الْحق}: Mujāhid read الحق in the nominative, making it a naʿt (adjective) of Allah (exalted be His mention); and the accusative is as a naʿt of الدين.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying {يغضوا من أَبْصَارهم}: مِن is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins), and is not partitive.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying غير أولي الإربة: whoever reads غير in the accusative makes it accusative as an exception or as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Whoever reads it in the genitive makes it a naʿt (adjective), because التابعين is not a genuinely definite noun with a specific referent, since it is not something known [to the hearer]. It may also be in the genitive as a badal (substitute). In both views it is like {غير المغضوب عَلَيْهِم}.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying {وَالَّذين يَبْتَغُونَ الْكتاب}: الَّذين is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "and among what is recited to you are those who seek the contract" (وَفِيمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُم الَّذين يَبْتَغُونَ الْكتاب). They may also be in the position of the accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "make a contract with those who seek the contract" (كاتبوا الَّذين يَبْتَغُونَ الْكتاب).

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying {مثل نوره كمشكاة}: مثل is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the kāf is the khabar (predicate). The hāʾ in نوره refers back to Allah (exalted be His mention); and it is said: to the Prophet (peace be upon him); and it is said: to faith in the heart of the believer.
His saying {دري}: whoever reads it with ḍamma on the dāl and a doubled yāʾ relates it to الدُّرّ (pearls) because of the excellence of its qualities, so it is فُعْلِيّ (a relative adjective). Its pattern may also be فُعِّيل, not a relative adjective, but derived from الدرء (repelling), with the hamza lightened so that it turned into a yāʾ, and the yāʾ before it was assimilated into it. As for whoever reads it with kasra on the dāl and with hamza (دِرِّيء), he makes it فِعِّيل from الدرء, on the pattern of فسيق and سكير; its meaning is that it drives away the darkness by its glittering and its light, so it is from درأت النجوم تدرأ, when the stars rush forth. As for whoever reads it with ḍamma on the dāl and with hamza (دُرِّيء), he makes it likewise فُعِّيل from درأت النجوم when they rush forth; and it is an adjective with few parallels: its parallel among nouns is المُرِّيق, and like it among adjectives are العُلِّيّة and السُّرِّيّة.

mekki-muskil:36-36.t: His saying {وَالْآصَال}: it is the plural of أُصُل, and أُصُل is the plural of أصيل, like رغيف and رُغُف. It is also said that the plural of الأصيل is أصائل; and it is said that أصائل is the plural of آصال.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying {فَاجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ جلدَة}: ثمانين is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and جلدة as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)); and likewise the accusative of {مائَة جلدَة}.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t:
His saying {ظلمات}: whoever reads it in the nominative takes it as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) من فوقه, or by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are darknesses" or "these are darknesses". Whoever reads it in the genitive makes it a badal (substitute) from the first ظلمات, and السحاب is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and من فوقه is the khabar.
His saying {لَا تحسبن الَّذين كفرُوا معجزين}: whoever reads it with yāʾ implies the agent, who is the Prophet (upon him be blessing and peace), and الذين and معجزين are the two objects of حسب. It is also possible that الذين are the agents, and you imply the first object of حسب, with معجزين the second; the implied form being "let not those who disbelieve think themselves able to escape" (لَا يَحسبن الَّذين كفرُوا أنفسهم معجزين). Whoever reads it with tāʾ, the Prophet (peace be upon him) is the agent, and {الَّذين} and {معجزين} are the two objects of حسب.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {كل قد علم صلَاته}: كلا is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and in علم is the pronoun of Allah (exalted be His mention). On this view it is permissible to make كل accusative by an implied verb which what follows it explains, its implied form being "Allah knows each one — He knows its prayer" (علم الله كلا علم صلَاته). If you make the pronoun in علم refer to كل, the accusative of كل becomes remote, because it is an agent whose action falls on something connected with it; so if you make it accusative by an implied verb, you make its action pass to itself. There is disagreement on this question, and there is room for consideration in it, because the agent has made its action pass to itself, and that is only permitted with verbs that enter upon the mubtadaʾ and khabar, like ظننت and علمت. This is the school of Sībawayh; so the accusative in كل, while it is the agent, is not permissible according to him, but is permissible according to the Kufans.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying {وَينزل من السَّمَاء من جبال فِيهَا من برد}: the second مِن is redundant (zāʾida) and the third مِن is for clarification (bayān); the implied form is "and He sends down from the sky mountains in it of hail" (وَينزل من السَّمَاء جبالا فِيهَا من برد), i.e. mountains of this kind. Al-Farrāʾ said: the implied form is "and He sends down from the sky, of mountains of hail" (وَينزل من السَّمَاء من جبال برد); so من برد according to al-Farrāʾ's view is in the position of the genitive, and according to the view of the Basrans in the position of the accusative as clarification or as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It has also been said that the third مِن is redundant and the implied form is "and He sends down from the sky, from mountains in it, hail" (وَينزل من السَّمَاء من جبال فِيهَا برد), i.e. He sends down hail from mountains in the sky. This indicates that in the sky there are mountains from which hail descends; while according to the first view it indicates that in the sky there are mountains of hail.
His saying {يذهب بالأبصار}: Abū Jaʿfar read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ of يُذهِب. This requires that the bāʾ not be brought, because it is a four-letter verb from أذهب, and the hamza alternates with the bāʾ [as a means of transitivity]. But al-Mubarrad and others permitted it on the basis that the bāʾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun), because the verb indicates it [Translator's note: the source reads يدل على اذ منه أخذ, evidently "indicates it, since it is taken from it"], its implied form being "it takes away, its taking away being with the sight" (يذهب ذَهَابه بالأبصار). On this basis they permitted أُدخِل بزيد السجن, as though he said "the prison was entered, an entering with Zayd" (أدخل السجن دخولا بزيد).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying إِلَّا الَّذين تَابُوا: الَّذين is in the position of the accusative as an exception; or, if you wish, in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in لهم.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {ويتقه}: whoever makes the qāf quiescent does so for lightness, as they said كَتْف for كَتِف. Whoever gives it kasra does so according to the origin, because the yāʾ after the qāf was dropped for the jussive.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {طَاعَة}: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "obedience is more fitting for you" (طَاعَة أولى بكم); or by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "our matter is obedience" (أمرنا طَاعَة). The accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) is permissible.

mekki-muskil:55-55.t:
His saying {وعد الله الَّذين آمنُوا}: the basic usage of وعد is that it takes two objects, and you may restrict it to one of them; for that reason it takes one object in this verse, and the promise is explained by His saying {ليَستَخْلِفنهم}, as the promise in al-Māʾida is explained by His saying {لَهُم مغْفرَة}, and as the injunction in al-Nisāʾ is explained by His saying {للذّكر مثل حَظّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ}.
His saying {يعبدونني}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from {الَّذين آمنُوا}, or in the position of the nominative as a break (qaṭʿ, a new sentence).

mekki-muskil:58-58.t:
His saying {ثَلَاث عورات}: whoever reads ثلاث in the accusative makes it a badal (substitute) from His saying {ثَلَاث مَرَّات}. {ثَلَاث مَرَّات} is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun); and it is said: because it is in the position of the maṣdar, not being a maṣdar in reality. It is also said that it is an adverb (ẓarf), its implied form being "three times", i.e. let them ask your permission at three times. This is more correct in meaning, because they were not commanded that slaves and children ask their permission three times; they were only commanded that they ask their permission at three times. Do you not see that He has explained the times, saying {من قبل صَلَاة الْفجْر وَحين تضعون ثيابكم من الظهيرة وَمن بعد صَلَاة الْعشَاء}? So He explained the three occasions by the times, and it is known that it is an adverb; and this is correct. So if it is an adverb, {ثَلَاث عورات} is substituted from it on the reading of whoever reads ثلاث عورات in the accusative. This substitution is not sound unless an omitted muḍāf is assumed, its implied form being "the times of three [periods of] privacy" (أَوْقَات ثَلَاث عورات); so you substitute "the times of three privacies" from "three times", and both are adverbs, so you substitute an adverb from an adverb, and the meaning and the i'rab are sound.
As for whoever reads ثلاث عورات in the nominative, he makes it the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "these are three privacies" (هَذِه ثَلَاث عورات), i.e. these are the times of three privacies; then the muḍāf was omitted by way of extension (ittisāʿ), and هذه points to the three times mentioned before this. But the speech was extended and the times were made "privacies", because the exposure of the private parts happens in them. It is like their saying نهارك صَائِم وليلك قَائِم ("your day is fasting and your night is standing in prayer"): you predicate fasting of the day because it happens in it, and standing of the night because it happens in it. From it is His saying, the Exalted, بل مكر اللَّيْل وَالنَّهَار: plotting is annexed [Translator's note: the source has أضبف for أضيف] to the night and the day, though they do not plot; but plotting happens in them on the part of those who do it, so the plotting was annexed to them by extension. Likewise you predicate "privacies" of the times, because in them [people's private parts] are exposed. For that reason Allah commanded His servants that no slave or child should enter upon them at these three times except after asking permission.
The original vowel of the wāw in العورات is fatḥa, but it was made quiescent so that the change [into alif] would not become necessary in it because it is vowelled and the letter before it has fatḥa; and like it is بيضات. This command from Allah to the believers was only because the houses were without doors.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying {إِلَّا أنفسهم}: nominative as a badal (substitute) from شهداء, which is the noun of كان, and {وَلَهُم} is the khabar. It is permissible to make شهداء accusative as the fronted khabar of كان, with {أنفسهم} its noun; and it is permissible to make أنفسهم accusative as an exception or as the khabar of كان, but it has not been read so.
His saying {فشهادة أحدهم أَربع شَهَادَات}: أربع is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and its governing word (ʿāmil) is شهادة. شهادة is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "so the ruling" or "so the obligation is the testimony of one of them four times" (فَالْحكم أو فالفرض شَهَادَة أحدهم أَربع مَرَّات), i.e. the ruling is that one of them testify four testimonies by Allah that he is of the truthful. It is also said that شهادة is nominative as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar (predicate) omitted, i.e. "so it is upon them" or "so it is binding on them that one of them testify four testimonies".
His saying {إِنَّه لمن الصَّادِقين}: in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of شهادة. إنّ was not given fatḥa because of the lām that is in the khabar, as in your saying علمت إن زيدا لمنطلق ("I knew that Zayd is surely departing").
And His saying {بِاللَّه}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) شهادات, so it is in its ṣila, if you make the second govern; and if you assume the governing of the first, which is شهادة, the bāʾ is attached to شهادة. Whoever reads أربع in the nominative takes it as the khabar of شهادة, as you say صَلَاة الظّهْر أَربع رَكْعَات ("the noon prayer is four rakʿas"), and بالله is then attached to شهادات; it may not be attached to شهادة, because you would be separating the ṣila from the mawṣūl (relative) by the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is أربع شهادات. And إنه لمن الصادقين is then attached to شهادات, and is not attached to شهادة, because of what we mentioned of separating the ṣila from the mawṣūl.

mekki-muskil:60-60.t:
His saying {وَالْقَوَاعِد}: it is the plural of قاعد in the relational sense (ʿalā al-nasab), i.e. one possessing sitting [i.e. past childbearing]; for that reason the hāʾ [of the feminine] was dropped. The Kufans said: since it applies only to the feminine, the hāʾ was dispensed with. It is also said that the hāʾ was dropped to distinguish between it and القاعدة in the meaning of "the one seated".
His saying {غير متبرجات}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يضعن; and it is said to be a ḥāl from هنّ in ثيابهن.
His saying {وَأَن يستعففن}: أن is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and {خير} is the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:61-61.t:
His saying {جَمِيعًا أَو أشتاتا}: both are ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in تأكلوا.
His saying {تَحِيَّة}: a maṣdar (verbal noun), because {فَسَلمُوا} means "then greet".

mekki-muskil:63-63.t:
His saying {كدعاء بَعْضكُم}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as the second object of جعل.
His saying {لِوَاذًا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); and it is said to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the meaning of "taking cover with one another" (ملاوذين). لواذا remained sound with the wāw because it is sound in لاوذ, and the maṣdar of فاعَل does not undergo weakening (iʿlāl).

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying {وَالْخَامِسَة}: nominative, conjoined to أربع in the reading of whoever reads it in the nominative, or as a break (qaṭʿ, a new sentence).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {أَن تشهد أَربع شَهَادَات}: nothing is good in أربع but the accusative by تشهد. أن is in the position of the nominative by يدرأ [as its agent], its implied form being "and her testifying four testimonies by Allah that he is of the liars averts the punishment from her" (وَيدْفَع عَنْهَا الْحَد شهادتها أَربع شَهَادَات بِاللَّه إنه لمن الْكَاذِبين). إنه and what follows it is in the position of the accusative by تشهد, and إنّ was given kasra because of the lām that is in the khabar [Translator's note: the source has الخير, evidently for الخبر]. And in بالله the bāʾ may well be attached to the first or the second.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t:
His saying {وَالْخَامِسَة}, which is the second one: whoever reads it in the accusative conjoins it to أربع شهادات, or [takes it] by an implied verb, its implied form being "and she testifies the fifth" (وَتشهد الْخَامِسَة). It is put in the place of the maṣdar (verbal noun), and its origin is an adjective set up in place of the qualified noun, as though He said "and she testifies the fifth testimony" (وَتشهد الشَّهَادَة الْخَامِسَة); then it was omitted [Translator's note: the source reads حذف الوجهين, "omitted the two aspects", as written]. Whoever reads it in the nominative takes it as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
His saying {أَن لعنة الله} and {أَن غضب الله}: أن and what follows it are in the position of the nominative as the khabar of الخامسة, if you make it nominative as a mubtadaʾ; or in the position of the accusative by the omission of the preposition, if you read {وَالْخَامِسَة} in the accusative. And الخامسة is an adjective standing in place of the qualified noun in the nominative, the implied form being "and the fifth testimony is that the curse of Allah be upon him" and "that the wrath of Allah be upon her". The bāʾ may not be attached to the omitted الشهادة, because you would be separating the ṣila from the mawṣūl by the description, and that is not permissible.
